searchText: kinna beside myself w/ excitement today for some reason. Really feels like everything is coming together 😄 Why are people going crazy over this: https://twitter.com/EdgarArout/status/1413149508611960839 https://twitter.com/EdgarArout/status/1413322294345097218 it's not like re-orgs are a new thing ? People don't actually listen to calmly delivered warnings from core devs, but they do listen to the ravings of an angry person on Twitter. 🙂 It is unfortunate because I don't think Edgar wants to break Ethereum, I think they just fail to realize how valuable of a protection it is to *not* build tools to break Ethereum. People are lazy and busy. If you have the ability to build something like this, you probably have better things to do with your time so no one does it. It is unclear why Edgar decided this was a good use of their time. the truth is that the community only pays attention to problems if something is a bout to burn down https://twitter.com/EdgarArout/status/1413230171176411136?s=19 probably forcing Devs to fix it The devs have been working on *mitigating* it for many years. It is an extremely hard problem and actively attacking Ethereum isn't going to speed things up. absolutely, this is a situation like Frankenstein's monster 🙃 Doing this in the waning days of PoW is even more dangerous, because miners' long term incentives are disappearing fast. There's no way you can claim this to be an act for the good of the ecosystem it only gets worse with PoS since validators are mostly anonymous and block proposers are known We can after-the-fact slash validators via social consensus though. We cannot after-the-fact slash individual miners. _via social consensus_ ... slashing people for issues that were ignored and still are to a degree sounds wrong to me 🙂 and you'd only get social consesus / support from validators that were not able to extract that kind of value The issues aren't ignored, there are just no known crytographic or economic solutions that don't sacrifice other desirable properties of Ethereum. Social consensus doesn't care about individual validators, or even the whole set. They care about the health of Ethereum. The whole idea with social consensus slashing is that the *users* of Ethereum have the ability to severely punish those who are in a privileged position (validators) should they act against the long term interest of Ethereum. It is the final backstop that allows us to deal with those problems we are unable to solved cryptoeconomically. A block proposer can't determine a successful fork by themselves though, without convincing enough of their committee. It's likely going to be much harder to get the attestations for a reorg in ETH2 than it is to get the hashrate for one now, isn't? In terms of number of actors you need to put together Things like increasing the gas limit + propose empty blocks, if you have a few block proposals in a row, to lower the base fee and get the best MEV reward. Actually, maybe there are some solutions with zkProofs in theory, but the tech is too new to implement it today on Ethereum. it's a toxic behaviour but not really a reason to get slashed? We will need a list of "please do not do this" I think there would be fair warning before a social consenus slashing. Asking nicely is step 1. 😀 With exception for egregious attacks like deep reorg double spends. right now, approximately 58% of the hashrate is by flashbots. I'm not sure how social consensus works, but what if they're the majority staked in eth2 as well? there will be infinite amount of MEV opportunities, where do you draw the line? more like 90+ iirc oh wow Does anyone have resources on social consensus? Social consensus here means end-users or their delegates installing a client update that includes an irregular state change that slashes certain misbehaving validators. These would be any validators who participated in an attack of the network, after the attack occurred. how is it decided if a state change is "irregular"? Essentially, the whole thing would occur outside of the normal ruleset, and it would require buy-in from the broader Ethereum community. An irregular state change is when an Ethereum execution clients update does a one-time mutation of the state trie outside of the normal EVM/consensus ruleset. hmm I see thanks <@301186049323958275> Ethereum has only done this once, with The DAO hardfork. 90% of hashrate is fine with getting paid by searchers, but I am not sure that translates to being fine with getting paid for reorgs, and I would assume many individual validators won't be ok with that, probably also exchanges since they have other business that needs a reputation to be maintained? It seems to me that the only way something like this happens *soon* in ETH2 is if it gets normalized and becomes considered just another component of the game > and I would assume many individual validators won't be ok with that why? Any resources on MEV-geth / alpha mining / flashbots / front running — I’m trying to understand this subject better. Do these bots cause congestion? https://discord.gg/BXpRvmCA https://github.com/flashbots/pm this is probably the place to start I am hoping many care enough about Ethereum to not participate in reorg auctions stakers are more aligned with the ecosystem than miners, so maybe that's true for enough of the stake that this wouldn't work? 🤔 you think binance for example is more aligned with the ecosystem? lol for some reason people think stakers are saints 🤣 No for that I mean small validators. As far as exchanges, I think doing reorgs is a different line to cross than extracting MEV, but maybe I am naive wait until everyone (stakers) gets a taste of the mev rewards <:MonkaChrist:770405693042720818> it’s human behavior, you are referring to the “i am here for the tech” people I think there's maybe one important difference between "normal" MEV extraction, which can be single-handedly done by a proposer, and this. The more validators decide extracting MEV isn't ethical, the more MEV they leave on the table and the faster the MEV extractors accrue power, both directly and through people wanting the higher yields and staking with them, so there's no way to mount opposition. Even a minority of extractors can grow very powerful fast. For this MEV from reorgs, it only works if you get enough validators on board that they can force the reorgs, or the game doesn't even start. You can't attract people with higher yields without having already gotten significant stake on board Performing re-orgs will be a lot more complicated on the beacon-chain as you have to pretty much bias the committee for that particular slot. sounds very naive to me, and we shouldn’t depend on the good faith of people it doesn't, because PoS has finalization, while mev reorg logic taken to the extreme can mean multi-hour reorgs. the next obvious step is to make a system to pay subsequent miners to build on top of your fork block (eg. by a contract that pays only if previous blockhash is X). effectively this becomes equivalent to renting majority of hashrate. PoW security based on just rewards is negligible maybe reorgs are not but there are 1000 different things you can do mev rewards without reorgs and multi block censorship are not a danger to the system imo, just a nuisance I wouldn't call it a nuisance because they are a centralization vector and also because harm to users at scale can be a systemic risk, but I agree with you that consensus instability is the greater problem, and harder to tackle all "MEV solutions" today have to do with protecting users or avoiding centralization, consensus instability is an afterthought at the moment The "it is fine unless it burns down"- approach is exactly what has gotten us here I don't think that's fair, and it goes back to the point about the different between reorgs and normal MEV. The latter you can't ignore, Flashbots might have accelerated things but it was in some sense necessary how? the problem is that PoW is fundamentally not secure. consensus risk is solved by PoS with slashing. in the medium term the plan is for ethereum to move to rollups, which is going to extinguish l1 mev honestly adopting this software would be a really dumb move by pools. if you are willing to reorg for money, just create a 51%+ cartel and extract mev without reorgs. this way you maximize income without damaging the system so much you could say the notion that a 51% cartel exists is more damaging to the system than some quick reorgs In order to be able to pull a successful reorg on the beacon-chain, the proposer needs to hold a majority of attesters on that slot that are willing to not follow rules regarding LMD Ghost vote. To not have it reverted in the next slot they'll need that as well. Any system you choose, no matter what form of proof you use, will be vulnerable to these attacks if a large majority of the players that are in charge of producing blocks, be it pow, pos or whatever, act in bad faith. Decentralization**is** a way of making this more difficult, but it does rely on the good faith of the majority. I guess the argument is that Flashbots could get a majority of validators just like they have almost all hashrate. I doubt they can for reorgs, but it's debatable Flashbots is an overlay rather than a core part of the protocol. Any attempt to use it for evil (as seen by the wider community) is likely to end up with it being forked or abandoned. why do you think that? Searchers will do whatever makes them the most $ but searchers only have as much power as the amount of stake/hashpower that is ok with what they do Because if the chain is seen as manipulable to a degree where finality is threatened it will lose value, so you may gain more ETH but less $. which is 90% now 😄 90% isn't on board for reorgs, just "normal" MEV which is unavoidable currently, if you don't extract it someone else will and it's the waning days of PoW with miners squeezing all profits before being gone Staking is also in general by consent: the big players are exchanges, banks, staking services _etc._ so if those who are staking with them believe the operator's actions are damaging Ethereum they may well decide to pull out and go somewhere else. okay, now what is "normal" mev extraction which happens in a block, 100% under the control of a single miner/proposer you don't need any coordination to extract it I can't agree. reorgs can destroy defi by censoring liquidations and/or price updates. consider a 30 minutes reorg that removes a price update, ending in such a state that you can borrow >$1 for $1 of collateral (using real prices). censorship is profitable as long as the defi protocol in question has any funds left. the coordination is already the flashbots relay a 51+% cartel that just uses its power to almost double its income is certainly preferable to this scenario. and uncle bandits have already happened fyi https://twitter.com/bertcmiller/status/1385294439569047562 that's why I think if this starts to become actually adopted it warrants an emergency merge. not sure what timeframe is realistic. PoS rewards will be significantly lower than current rewards, it will be a 4x (?) iirc I meant a 51+ PoW cartel vs most of hashrate adopting reorg mev code Isn't that where a block became an uncle, and the searcher pulled the txs from it so they could put them in to the next valid block? That's different from actively creating uncles or carrying out reorgs and pools like Rocketpool where you only need 16eth to run a validator decrease your stake as well it's a different kind of coordination. Any miner could extract this MEV by themselves, they only use Flashbots because it's easier and makes more money yeah, but it can happen, that was my point kind of 🙂 it's actually not really coordination among miners, they coordinate with searchers exchanges like binance run validators on polygon/eth/.../their own CEX -- they will MEV left and right and can offer
